findings.message: Statement uses Resource:*. Its resource scope is broad for the listed actions; it does not grant unlisted actions or establish effective access. Some actions require this scope.
findings.remediation: Check each listed action's resource-level support. Where supported, use specific ARNs or applicable resource-tag conditions; otherwise review service-specific conditions and required context.

findings.message: iam:PassRole without iam:PassedToService condition. An agent with unconstrained PassRole can escalate privileges by passing a high-privilege role to any service it can invoke.
findings.remediation: Add a Condition: {StringEquals: {iam:PassedToService: 'bedrock.amazonaws.com'}} (or whichever service runs the agent). Also restrict the Resource to specific role ARNs.
assumptions: Patterns are review signals, not effective permissions or proven exploitability.

SCPs, boundaries, session/resource policies and condition semantics are unknown.

findings.message: Agent has privilege-management action 'iam:PassRole'. This lets the agent modify IAM policies, create roles, or assume other identities - classic escalation path.
findings.remediation: Separate agent runtime roles from IAM administration. Agent runtime identities should NEVER have iam:* or policy-modification permissions.

findings.message: Statement has Resource: '*' and zero Condition keys. Agent policies should use conditions for tenant isolation (aws:PrincipalTag), request scoping (aws:RequestedRegion), or session binding (aws:TokenIssueTime).
findings.remediation: Add at minimum: aws:RequestedRegion to limit geographic blast radius, and aws:PrincipalTag/tenant for multi-tenant isolation.
